subject: Uptime anchoring and rolling credit proposal
messages:
From: Arjun Mehta <arjun@stratuspay.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: Kara Lim <kara@stratuspay.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Uptime anchoring and rolling credit proposal

Hannah —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We reviewed Redwood's SLA framework internally and want to propose an adjustment to the standard uptime anchor for our onboarding period. Our engineering constraints for the first 90 days of traffic ramp mean we can't comfortably guarantee 99.9% without a larger committed capacity investment.

Proposed ask from StratusPay:
- Temporary uptime anchor = 99.7% for the first 3 months post-launch (then revert to standard 99.9%).
- Monthly remedy: rolling credits applied to invoice for availability below the anchor, with bands:
  - 99.7% - 99.5% => 5% of monthly invoice
  - 99.5% - 99.0% => 12% of monthly invoice
  - <99.0% => 25% of monthly invoice
- Maintenance carveouts: standard scheduled maintenance windows (we expect one 2-hour weekly window) to be excluded from uptime measurements during the pilot.

We included a draft SOW (attached) with estimated traffic profiles and would like to keep commercial exposure limited while we validate traffic patterns. Happy to discuss but curious whether Redwood would consider a rolling-credit model rather than fixed caps for the first quarter.

Thanks,
Arjun
Director of Platform Engineering
StratusPay

Attachments: SOW-draft.pdf (1.2MB)

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
To: Arjun Mehta <arjun@stratuspay.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 11:38:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Uptime anchoring and rolling credit proposal

Arjun —

Appreciate the clear ask and the SOW — that's helpful context. We can be flexible for an initial ramp but want to make sure commercial terms and operational guardrails balance risk for both sides. A few clarifying points and a counter-proposal below.

Quick clarifications:
- Can you confirm expected launch date and projected Q1 peak RPS? (SOW had ranges but we need a single conservative number for sizing).
- Is the weekly 2-hour maintenance predictable (same day/time) or will it vary? Predictable windows are easier to carve out operationally.

Redwood counter-proposal: phased uptime anchoring + capped rolling credits
- Phase 1 (Month 0–2 after launch): anchor at 99.8% (instead of 99.7%) to reduce tail risk.
- Phase 2 (Month 3): anchor moves to 99.9% once we confirm traffic and KV cache hit rates.
- Remedy bands (monthly invoice credits):
  - 99.8% - 99.5% => 7.5% invoice credit
  - 99.5% - 99.0% => 15% invoice credit
  - <99.0% => 30% invoice credit
- Monthly credit cap: 20% of that month's invoice (rolling, not cumulative).
- Latency SLO: for production traffic over 95th percentile, p95 should be <= 400ms for standard endpoints; we can define a separate latency remedy if latency regressions materially impact availability.
- Maintenance carveout: we can agree to exclude one predictable 2-hour weekly window; additional windows require a 7-day notification.

I've attached a simple credit-template (credit-template-v1.xlsx) that maps how the monthly credit would apply against invoice line items under different bands. Ben/Laura — flagged you both for legal/commercial and billing ops input.

If that seems reasonable to you, can we schedule a 30-minute call this week to lock the numbers and route to legal for a short amendment?

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Arjun / team —

Quick commercial/legal notes from my side:
- We can accept a time-boxed deviation from standard uptime, but we'll need the following to limit Redwood's exposure:
  1) A defined pilot capacity (committed GPU-hour or RPS band) for the 90-day window so we can reserve autoscaling headroom.
  2) A monthly credit cap (Hannah suggested 20%) — we recommend lowering to 15% for the pilot if StratusPay cannot commit to a minimal reserved capacity.
  3) Clear rollback triggers that move you to the full 99.9% SLA early if sustained traffic exceeds the pilot band for two consecutive weeks.

Operationally, the weekly 2-hour carveout is fine so long as it's scheduled and communicated. Unscheduled maintenance that causes >30 min downtime should not be eligible for carveout.

If you accept those guardrails, legal can draft a short amendment rather than reworking the full Master Services Agreement. For speed, we can do DocuSign for the SOW + amendment once we finalize numbers.

Ben Carter
VP, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Hannah/Ben/Laura —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the counter-proposal. We discussed Ben's suggested guardrails and are prepared to accept the pilot constraints with one tweak:
- Monthly credit cap at 18% instead of 15% or 20% (splitting the difference).

We confirm target launch date: 2027-01-10. Conservative sizing for Q1 peak: 1,500 RPS. The weekly maintenance window will be Thursdays 02:00–04:00 PST and is predictable.

Please route a short amendment to the SOW reflecting Phase 1 = Months 0–2 at 99.8% anchor, monthly remedy bands as you proposed, monthly cap = 18%, and the reserved pilot capacity note. Once we have that, Kara and I will sign via DocuSign.

I'll wait for the amendment link. Appreciate the flexibility — happy to run a smoke test the week of Jan 3rd if that helps validate the rollout plan.

Best,
Arjun
Director of Platform Engineering
StratusPay
